messages.author: 253a4e0713b4882c
messages.subject: Interpreting ProcD.lm pairwise comparisons
parts:
Hi everyone, I've been out of the geomorph scene for a while, and I wanted to make sure I'm interpreting the new functions correctly.

I've got two horse taxa, and two tooth types, premolars and molars. And I'm seeing if I can differentiate them.

Here is the code I used for just tooth type:

gdf <- geomorph.data.frame(procrustes, taxon = metadata$Taxon, PM=metadata$PM)

fit.full.PM <- procD.lm(coords ~ PM, data=gdf, iter=9999)
PW.PM <- pairwise(fit.full.PM, groups=PM, covariate=NULL)
summary(PW.PM, test.type="dist", confidence=0.95, stat.table=T)

Pairwise distances between means, plus statistics
            d              UCL (95%) Z              Pr > d
M:P 0.0635135 0.04223325 4.439552  2e-04

So it looks like molars and premolars are different, fantastic!

Then next, are the taxa different.

fit.full.taxon <- procD.lm(coords ~ taxon, data = gdf, iter = 9999, print.progress = FALSE)
PW.taxon <- pairwise(fit.full.taxon, groups=taxon, covariate=NULL)
summary(PW.taxon, test.type="dist", confidence=0.95, stat.table=T)

Pairwise distances between means, plus statistics
                                           d                UCL (95%)        Z     Pr > d
Equus:Haringtonhippus 0.08455865 0.0422617 6.893069  1e-04

They are, wonderful!

So now tooth position by taxa.

gp <- interaction(gdf$taxon, gdf$PM)

fit.full <- procD.lm(coords ~ taxon * PM, data=gdf, iter=9999)
PW <- pairwise(fit.full, groups=gp, covariate=NULL)
summary(PW, test.type="dist", confidence=0.95, stat.table=T)

Pairwise distances between means, plus statistics
                                                                      d              UCL (95%)          Z      Pr > d
Equus.M:Haringtonhippus.M                0.08398799 0.11229488 -0.4071530 0.6495
Equus.M:Equus.P                                 0.05874994 0.08389465 -1.2155296 0.8873
Equus.M:Haringtonhippus.P                 0.10621708 0.13094403 -0.1636174 0.5558
Haringtonhippus.M:Equus.P                 0.10741843 0.12865578 -0.3249280 0.6215
Haringtonhippus.M:Haringtonhippus.P 0.07946212 0.08920087  0.7698235 0.2180
Equus.P:Haringtonhippus.P                 0.09160541 0.11116093  0.2079084 0.4069

So now nothing is different. Even molars of one taxon with premolars of the other taxon.

I'm not sure how to interpret this. If the teeth are different, and the taxa are different, it seems odd that the combinations wouldn't also be different.
I'm sure I must be missing something. If anyone has any advice I would appreciate it.

I've attached a screenshot of the summary results in case the email formatting messes it up.

Thank you!

messages.author: aab55242ff4da6c6
messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Interpreting ProcD.lm pairwise comparisons
parts:
What if you perform ANOVA on fit.full?

anova(fit.full)

I am willing to bet the interaction term is not significant.  Your pairwise test - without providing a specific null model - will use the one inherent in fit full.  This can be revealed with

reveal.model.designs(fit.full)

Remember that pairwise tests must use a null model as a basis for the test and if there is little variation in the taxon*PM interaction, there will be no significant differences, given taxon and PM differences; i.e., the difference in PM is consistent between taxa.

Cheers!
Mike

messages.subject: Re: [geomorph-r-package] Interpreting ProcD.lm pairwise comparisons
parts:
You can force the pairwise analysis to have a null model that has only an intercept, like it was in the first two tests you performed (see the help page and/or the vignette).  Then you will likely find out all means are different, given that null model.   It depends on the question you are asking.

Mike
